title: Chicken Lo Mein
subtitle: chewy egg noodles tossed with tender chicken, carrots and cabbage in a savoury-sweet soy sauce
imageAlt: Glossy brown lo mein noodles with sliced chicken, carrots and cabbage in a cream bowl
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, cornstarch

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen chicken? Thaw it in the fridge overnight.
Put a big pot of water on to boil for the noodles.
Have everything cut and the sauce mixed before you turn on the pan — it cooks fast.

items.name: lo mein or fresh egg noodles

steps.title: Coat the chicken
steps.text: Toss the chicken strips with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp cornstarch. Set aside while you prep.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, water, cornstarch, ginger and pepper in a jug.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Boil the noodles 1 minute less than the package says (fresh lo mein: 2–3 minutes). Drain, rinse briefly with warm water and toss with a few drops of oil so they don't clump.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high. Cook the chicken in a single layer 2–3 minutes per side until golden and 74°C (165°F). Move to a plate.

steps.title: Stir-fry the veg
steps.text: Add the last 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry the onion and carrots 2 minutes, then the coleslaw mix and garlic 1–2 minutes until just wilted.

steps.title: Toss it all
steps.text: Add the noodles, chicken and sauce. Toss with tongs 1–2 minutes until every noodle is glossy and coated. Serve right away.

fixIt.fix: Rinse them after draining and toss with a little oil; separate with tongs before they hit the pan.
Use low-sodium soy sauce, and add a splash of water and a pinch of sugar.
Add 2–3 tbsp water or broth and toss over the heat.
Add 1 more tbsp oyster sauce — it's the backbone of takeout flavour.

saleTip: Coleslaw mix is the cheapest pre-cut stir-fry veg at No Frills (~$2.50). Look for lo mein or fresh egg noodles in the produce cooler or international aisle.
swap: Beef, pork or shrimp instead of chicken. Spaghetti or linguine work if you can't find lo mein noodles.
leftovers: Fridge 3–4 days. One of the best lunch leftovers in the book.
source: Based on tested takeout-style lo mein methods (The Woks of Life, Damn Delicious): soy + oyster sauce base, noodles par-cooked and tossed in a very hot wok.
prepAhead: Slice the chicken and veg a day ahead.
Mix the sauce up to 3 days ahead.
reheat: Microwave covered 2 minutes with a splash of water, tossing halfway, until steaming (74°C / 165°F), or toss in a hot skillet.

basic.note: Chicken and noodles with soy sauce, sugar and garlic.

stepNotes.1: Basic: soy sauce, brown sugar, water, cornstarch and pepper.

fancy.note: Glossy restaurant lo mein with honey, sesame and crisp-tender veg.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: whisk the honey into the sauce.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: add the peas with the coleslaw mix.

plating: Twist the noodles high with tongs in the centre of the plate.

why.1-1: Oyster sauce gives the deep takeout flavour.
why.1-3: Sesame oil is the takeout aroma — a little goes far.
why.2-0: Rinsing the noodles stops them clumping.

funFact: Lo mein means “stirred noodles” in Cantonese: the noodles are boiled, then tossed with sauce. Chow mein means “fried noodles”, which are fried until crisp.
